members.name: Gina Ponce
members.backstory: Gina played bass in wedding bands for twelve years and could fake any song by the second chorus. They have perfect pitch and a left ear that rings constantly. Gina grew up in Des Moines, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Salihu, Gina's friend, carried Gina home once, no questions. Gina learned patching people up watching Salihu dose Gina's fever with willow bark tea, not aspirin.

members.name: Rabiu Sule
members.backstory: Rabiu grew soy and sweet corn on two hundred acres. They know soil by smell and weather by the ache in their knees. This ground is strange, but ground is ground. Rabiu grew up in Zaria, red laterite roads, yam farms, and markets bigger than towns. Aisha, Rabiu's grandchildren, are with their other grandparent, or were. members.name: Luis Fernandez
members.backstory: Luis was a mason — stone, brick, block, in that order of love. He has laid walls that will outlive his grandchildren. His grandparents came from Portland; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Victor's crew. Lays stone like he's writing.

members.name: Farid Ahmed
members.backstory: Farid the locksmith could open anything except a conversation about fees. He has a feather touch and a shop full of key blanks older than his customers. His grandparents came from Medellín; he grew up hearing Spanish at home, and still understand more than he can say. Can open anything. Chooses not to, mostly.

members.name: Emma Larsen
members.backstory: Emma ran a small-animal clinic in Oslo and a weekend large-animal route. She has stitched up everything from parakeets to draft horses. Her parents came from Denver; she grew up hearing English at home. Treats people like nervous animals. It works.

members.name: David Kim
members.backstory: David was the plumber everyone called when the other plumbers gave up. He has a sixth sense for where water goes when it shouldn't. His parents came from Houston; he grew up hearing English at home. Water is water. He'll find it, move it, or apologize to it.

members.name: Victor Lopez
members.backstory: Victor restored a hundred-year-old courthouse, matching mortar the old men forgot. He keeps a trowel older than his marriage and treat both with respect. His parents came from rural England; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Builds. That's it. He builds.

members.name: Rafael Torres

members.name: Daniyar Askarov
members.backstory: Daniyar ran 911 calls for six years. He has seen people at their worst and their bravest, often in the same hour. The clearing is just another scene to work. Talks slower when things are bad. People notice, and calm down. He was seen tipping salt from a pouch in a thin line across the shelter doorway before bed. When asked he shrugged: old habit, keeps the bad dreams on the other side.
